name: How do you budget a family-room addition with a contingency?

mainEntity.name: How much extra money should homeowners set aside for hidden issues during construction?
mainEntity.text: How much extra money should homeowners set aside for hidden issues during construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contingency is essential in a family-room addition budget because hidden conditions are common once walls, floors, and foundations are opened up. Older Los Angeles homes may reveal outdated wiring, termite damage, weak framing, moisture issues, or unanticipated structural modifications. Without a contingency, those surprises can stall the project or force lower-quality compromises. Homeowners should ask for a budget that includes all major soft costs and a reserve for unforeseen conditions. This reserve is not wasted money; it protects the schedule and keeps the project from becoming a stop-start experience. A well-planned contingency makes it easier to respond to surprises without sacrificing the core design goals.
